units.rhetorical_move: purpose clause, then the two risky assets and the one risk-free asset, then the two tests announced before any method
units.function: open a summary by naming the goal, the assets, and the tests the reader will meet
units.reusable_pattern: In order to [goal], we set up [object] for [assets]. The [tests] are carried out on it.
prohibited_generalizations: do not open a summary with the result
do not name assets the paper never trades
units.source_excerpt: In order to obtain higher investment returns and minimize risks, We strive to establish the optimal investment strategy model

features.transition: First, Considering that, Then, On this basis
original_instantiations: To keep bread fresh longer, we built a storage plan for loaves, rolls, and a tin of dry crackers. Freshness checks and taste checks were both run on it.
To keep a table steady, we built a bracing plan for the legs, the apron, and the top. Load checks and wobble checks were both run on it.

units.rhetorical_move: four connectors in one paragraph, each handing the reader the next piece: First, Considering that, Then, On this basis
units.function: walk a pipeline in one paragraph without a numbered list
units.reusable_pattern: First, [step]. Considering that [cost], [decision]. Then, [measure]. On this basis, [model].
prohibited_generalizations: do not use the chain where the steps are independent
do not add a connector the paragraph does not need
units.source_excerpt: First, we use the ARIMA algorithm ... Considering that too frequent transactions will increase transaction costs

features.transition: First, Considering that, Then, On this basis
original_instantiations: First, warm the milk. Because a cold dough rises slowly, set the bowl near the stove. Then knead. On that basis, shape the loaf.
First, cut the board. Because a dull blade tears the grain, sharpen it. Then drill. On that basis, glue the joint.

units.rhetorical_move: the only numbers in the paragraph come after the method, three of them, closed by a which-proves clause
units.function: put the quantitative payload at the end of the method paragraph and bind it to one claim
units.reusable_pattern: Bringing [data] into the model, we find [three returns], which proves that [claim].
prohibited_generalizations: do not spread the returns across the paragraph
do not let the proof clause claim more than the three numbers support
units.source_excerpt: a 5-year total investment return of 616.63%, an average annual return of 261.41%, and a maximum annual return of 664.69%, which proves

features.transition: First, Considering that, Then, On this basis
original_instantiations: Putting the dough in the oven, we found a rise of one third, a crumb with even holes, and a crust of even color, which shows the loaf baked well.
Putting the frame under load, we found a sag of one millimeter, joints that held, and legs that stayed square, which shows the frame was sound.

units.rhetorical_move: Second shifts from building to proving, and the test is reported as bounds rather than as the raw values
units.function: report a test by the bound it clears, not by the table
units.reusable_pattern: Second, we prove [claim]. In the [test], the [metric] are all [bound] and close to [limit].
prohibited_generalizations: do not quote the bound when the table gives a single value the reader needs
do not say close to a limit the paper never names
units.source_excerpt: the MAPE values are all less than 0.1 and very close to 0 and the R2-score are all greater than 94% and close to 1

features.transition: First, Considering that, Then, On this basis
original_instantiations: Second, we checked the bake. In the color test, every loaf came out deep gold, close to the color card.
Second, we checked the glue. In the strength test, every joint held firm, close to the rated load.

units.rhetorical_move: the performance test is told as behavior: buy early, hold, survive the fall
units.function: state what the strategy does in a market regime before giving its number
units.reusable_pattern: the model can [action] in the [regime], [hold], and [grasp]. Meanwhile, the model [survives] the [other regime].
prohibited_generalizations: do not narrate behavior the figure does not show
do not reuse Meanwhile for a contrast that is not simultaneous
units.source_excerpt: the investment model can buy in the early stage of the bull market, hold it to rise, and accurately grasp the profit opportunities

features.transition: First, Considering that, Then, On this basis
original_instantiations: The baker can start the loaf early, leave it to rise, and catch the moment it springs. Meanwhile, the same bake survives a cool kitchen.
The carpenter can cut the tenon early, leave it to seat, and catch the moment it locks. Meanwhile, the same joint survives a damp shed.

units.rhetorical_move: a disturbance test closes on a one-sided comparison and a two-goal clause
units.function: compare a strategy with its disturbed copies and close on both goals at once
units.reusable_pattern: [disturbances] generate [count] groups. [Their] return is lower, and ours is higher than [percent] of them, which proves [two goals] at the same time.
prohibited_generalizations: do not treat a one-sided comparison as a statistical test
do not claim both goals when only one was measured
units.source_excerpt: the 5-year total return of our investment strategy is higher than 93% of the simulated investment strategies, which proves that our investment model can maximize profit and minimize risk at the same time

features.transition: First, Considering that, Then, On this basis
original_instantiations: Small changes to the recipe gave 12 trial loaves. Their rise was lower, and ours beat 10 of them, which shows the recipe gives both volume and an even crumb at once.
Small changes to the joint gave 12 trial frames. Their stiffness was lower, and ours beat 10 of them, which shows the joint gives both strength and a clean look at once.

units.rhetorical_move: the sensitivity paragraph gives one concrete pair, then a direction with no number, then a floor
units.function: lead a sensitivity claim with the one pair that moves most, then the direction, then the floor
units.reusable_pattern: We test [object]. [Input] down [amount], [output] up [amount]. In addition, [direction]. Finally, [floor].
prohibited_generalizations: do not invent the second number of the pair
do not drop the floor when the paper gives one
units.source_excerpt: the transaction cost of bitcoin decreases by 1%, and the 5-year average annual investment rate of return increases by 1.75%

features.transition: First, Considering that, Then, On this basis
original_instantiations: We test how the loaf reacts to salt. Salt down by a pinch, the rise up by a finger. Also, the dough reacts more to less salt than to more. At the end, every trial still cleared the pan.
We test how the joint reacts to glue. Glue down by a drop, the hold up by a notch. Also, the joint reacts more to less glue than to more. At the end, every trial still held the shelf.

units.rhetorical_move: a general habit, then the person who faces it, then the object they build
units.function: open an introduction from a habit everyone shares down to the person in the problem
units.reusable_pattern: People are always [habit], and when faced with [decision], [person] must [act].
prohibited_generalizations: do not open on a habit the paper never connects to the task
do not stay at the general level past the first sentence
units.source_excerpt: People are always looking for good investment methods to improve their asset status, and when faced with investment decisions, market traders must seek the best opportunity

original_instantiations: People always want a warm meal, and when supper is late, the cook must find the fastest dish.
People always want a level floor, and when the boards rock, the carpenter must find the worst spot.

units.rhetorical_move: a how-to question names the core problem, then an authority with a year converts the question into a tool
units.function: pose the problem as a question and answer it with one named source and its year
units.reusable_pattern: For any [object], how to [balance] is the core problem. [Name] put forward [theory] in [year]. This provides [basis].
prohibited_generalizations: do not cite an authority the model never uses
do not give the year without the use
units.source_excerpt: The famous American economist Harry Markowitz systematically put forward the Portfolio Theory in 1952. This provides a theoretical basis

original_instantiations: For any stew, how to balance richness and cost is the hard part. Auguste Escoffier set down the mother sauces in 1903. That gives a cook a place to start.
For any shelf, how to balance strength and weight is the hard part. Thomas Chippendale set down his cabinet patterns in 1754. That gives a maker a place to start.

units.rhetorical_move: First, in this case, turns the theory into the assignment and names the data and the horizon
units.function: restate the task with the data it may use and the period it must cover
units.reusable_pattern: First, in this case, we need to [build] based on [data], which can provide [deliverable] for [horizon].
prohibited_generalizations: do not restate a task the problem never set
do not add data the paper does not have
units.source_excerpt: we need to develop a mathematical model for traders investing in both assets based on the past stream of daily prices of gold and bitcoin

original_instantiations: First, for this order, we need a recipe for a family of four, drawn from the pantry list, which can feed them for a week.
First, for this job, we need a cutting list for a bookcase, drawn from the timber in the rack, which can fill the wall.

units.rhetorical_move: a second sentence adds the commission with According to, and no new number marker
units.function: add one constraint the theory requires, inside the same task, without opening a new item
units.reusable_pattern: According to [theory], we must consider [benefits] and [risks], and [constraint] should also be taken into account.
prohibited_generalizations: do not promote the added constraint into its own task
do not cite the theory for a constraint it does not imply
units.source_excerpt: According to the idea of Portfolio Theory, we must comprehensively consider the benefits and risks, and the impact of the commission

original_instantiations: Following the classic method, we must watch both flavor and texture, and the cost of butter should also be counted.
Following the shop standard, we must watch both strength and appearance, and the cost of hardwood should also be counted.

units.rhetorical_move: Second gives the reason before the task: confidence first, demonstration second
units.function: state why a proof is owed before stating the proof
units.reusable_pattern: Second, in order to [build confidence], we need to demonstrate that [claim].
prohibited_generalizations: do not put the reason after the demonstration when the paper leads with it
do not claim confidence the paper only promises
units.source_excerpt: Second, in order to build traders' confidence in our model, we need to demonstrate in some way that the strategy provided by our model is the most effective

original_instantiations: Second, so the family trusts the baking, we need to show in some way that this loaf keeps.
Second, so the client trusts the work, we need to show in some way that this joint holds.

units.rhetorical_move: Then attaches the sensitivity task to the proof task with as, giving the factor and then the need
units.function: join a second deliverable to the one before it by the factor that makes it necessary
units.reusable_pattern: Then, as [factor] is one of the important factors affecting [decision], we need to [find a test].
prohibited_generalizations: do not split the joined deliverable into its own section opener
do not reverse the factor and the result beyond what the paper prints
units.source_excerpt: as commission for transaction is one of the important factors affecting investment decisions, we need to find a sensitivity test method

original_instantiations: Then, since oven heat is one thing that changes the crumb, we need a way to test it.
Then, since shop humidity is one thing that changes the glue, we need a way to test it.

units.rhetorical_move: Finally names the letter, its page limit, and the three things it must show
units.function: close a restatement with the communication artifact, its length, and its contents
units.reusable_pattern: Finally, we need to provide [reader] with a [artifact] of [limit] showing [three items].
prohibited_generalizations: do not state a page limit the problem never set
do not add an item the letter does not carry
units.source_excerpt: Finally, we need to provide traders with a memorandum of less than two pages showing the results of our work, including our model, the investment strategy derived from the model, and an analysis of the results

original_instantiations: Finally, we owe the client a note of under a page covering the recipe, the batch it produced, and how it tasted.
Finally, we owe the client a note of under a page covering the joint, the frame it produced, and how it held.

units.rhetorical_move: one sentence hands the reader to the figure and stops
units.function: let a figure carry the work plan instead of restating it in prose
units.reusable_pattern: The [figure] of the work in this paper is shown as follows.
prohibited_generalizations: do not retell the figure in the sentence that introduces it
do not use the handover where the figure is missing
units.source_excerpt: The flow chart of the work in this paper is shown as follows.

original_instantiations: The layout of the bench is shown below.
The layout of the shop is shown below.

units.rhetorical_move: a frame sentence names two sources for the assumptions: the actual situation and classical theory
units.function: say where the assumptions come from before listing them
units.reusable_pattern: In order to [purpose], we make the following assumptions according to [source] and [source].
prohibited_generalizations: do not claim a source the assumptions do not use
do not skip the frame and start at the bullets
units.source_excerpt: we make the following assumptions and simplifications according to the actual situation and classical theory

original_instantiations: To make the bake repeatable, we set the following rules from the kitchen we have and from standard practice.
To make the build repeatable, we set the following rules from the timber we have and from shop practice.

units.rhetorical_move: each bullet starts with Assuming that, and the two preference bullets share a when-faced-with frame
units.function: give every assumption the same opener, and pair the two that mirror each other
units.reusable_pattern: Assuming that [rule]. Assuming that [person], when faced with two alternatives, will choose [one]. Assuming that [person], when faced with two alternatives, will choose [the other].
prohibited_generalizations: do not merge the mirrored pair into one bullet
do not drop the when-faced-with frame on only one of them
units.source_excerpt: Assuming that traders are all risk averters. When faced with two alternatives, and other things are equal, they will choose the portfolio with less risk.

original_instantiations: We take it that the oven holds its heat. We take it that the cook, given two tins, picks the lighter one. We take it that the cook, given two tins, picks the taller one.
We take it that the bench stays flat. We take it that the maker, given two boards, picks the stiffer one. We take it that the maker, given two boards, picks the lighter one.

units.rhetorical_move: the table is introduced in one sentence, and a second sentence defers the rare symbols
units.function: point at the notation table and promise to define the rest at first use
units.reusable_pattern: In this work, we use the nomenclature in [table]. Other [rare] symbols will be introduced once they are used.
prohibited_generalizations: do not define a symbol in prose that the table already owns
do not defer a symbol the model uses immediately
units.source_excerpt: we use the nomenclature in Table 1 in the model construction. Other nonefrequent-used symbols will be introduced once they are used.

original_instantiations: Here the names in the chart are the ones we build with. Any rare name is explained the first time it appears.
Here the names in the chart are the ones we cut with. Any rare name is explained the first time it appears.

units.rhetorical_move: the count of missing values comes first, then the dates, then the reason, then the fill rule
units.function: justify a fill by the calendar fact that explains the gap
units.reusable_pattern: First of all, we observe [count] missing values. The dates are [calendar]. Based on [situation], we consider [reason]. For [convenience], we set [fill].
prohibited_generalizations: do not fill a gap the paper leaves empty
do not give the rule before the count
units.source_excerpt: there are 10 missing values in the gold price data. The dates corresponding to the missing values are the working day or the previous working day on Christmas Eve and New Year's Eve

features.transition: First of all, It can be seen
original_instantiations: To begin, we found 4 gaps in the bake log. The gaps fall on the days the oven was serviced. Given that, we treat them as days with no bake, and we copy the previous day's note.
To begin, we found 4 gaps in the cut list. The gaps fall on the days the saw was serviced. Given that, we treat them as days with no cutting, and we copy the previous day's note.

units.rhetorical_move: a figure is read for one contrast: one series changed more, and the two ranges are given
units.function: state the contrast a pair of charts supports and attach the two ranges
units.reusable_pattern: It can be seen from [figures] that [both] changed greatly, and especially [one] changed more. The range for [one] is [value] and the range for [the other] is [value].
prohibited_generalizations: do not quote a range the axis does not support
do not say especially when the ranges are close
units.source_excerpt: the prices of gold and Bitcoin have changed greatly in the past five years, and especially the price of Bitcoin has changed more dramatically

features.transition: First of all, It can be seen
original_instantiations: The two charts show that both doughs grew, and the rye grew more. One spans a hand's width, the other a thumb's width.
The two charts show that both boards moved, and the pine moved more. One spans a finger's width, the other a hair's width.

units.rhetorical_move: a second figure is read as two observations and closed with This shows
units.function: read a diagnostic chart into one conclusion sentence
units.reusable_pattern: We can see that [observation] and [observation]. This shows that [conclusion].
prohibited_generalizations: do not draw a conclusion the chart does not show
do not stack a second conclusion onto the same this-shows
units.source_excerpt: the standard deviation of the sequence {bt} is much larger than that of the sequence {gt}, and the absolute value of the correlation coefficient is relatively large

features.transition: First of all, It can be seen
original_instantiations: We can see the rye varies more than the wheat, and the two move together. This shows the rye is the lively one, and the two doughs rise as a pair.
We can see the pine varies more than the oak, and the two move together. This shows the pine is the lively one, and the two boards move as a pair.

units.rhetorical_move: the model is introduced by what it analyzes, where it is used, and the property that follows
units.function: justify a model choice by the property the series needs
units.reusable_pattern: The [model] analyzes [object] and is often used in [field]. It describes [property], and therefore has [ability]. After considering [alternatives], we choose it.
prohibited_generalizations: do not claim the model was compared with alternatives the paper does not name
do not attribute an ability the paper does not tie to the property
units.source_excerpt: The ARIMA model describes the short-term memory of sequences based on the autocorrelation of time-series data, and therefore has short-term predictive properties.

original_instantiations: A poolish is a preferment bakers use for long ferments. It keeps a memory of the last fold, and so it predicts the next rise. After comparing preferments, we chose it.
A sliding dovetail is a joint cabinetmakers use for long cases. It keeps a memory of the last cut, and so it predicts the next fit. After comparing joints, we chose it.

units.rhetorical_move: three parameters are glossed in one sentence, in the order p, d, q is not: d first, then p, then q
units.function: gloss every symbol of a named model in the order the paper uses, not the alphabetical order
units.reusable_pattern: In the [model], [symbol] is [meaning], [symbol] is [meaning], and [symbol] is [meaning].
prohibited_generalizations: do not reorder the gloss to match a textbook
do not add a symbol the model statement omits
units.source_excerpt: d is the number of differences made to change the time series into a stationary series, p is the lag order of the sequence, and q is the lag order of the random error term

original_instantiations: In this bake, the folds set how many times the dough is turned, the rest sets how long it sits, and the salt sets how tight it gets.
In this joint, the depth sets how far the cut goes, the width sets how wide it opens, and the angle sets how the faces meet.

units.rhetorical_move: a numbered step states what is seen in the figures, adds a second test, and closes with therefore
units.function: stack the visible evidence and the formal test, then conclude the series is not ready
units.reusable_pattern: First, we perform [test]. It can be seen from [figures] that [evidence]. At the same time, [second test]. Therefore [conclusion].
prohibited_generalizations: do not conclude non-stationarity from a figure alone when the paper also cites a test
do not drop the second test
units.source_excerpt: the two time series have obvious trends, and the decay speed of the autocorrelation coefficient is relatively slow. At the same time, we also conduct a Unit Root Test

original_instantiations: First, we checked the dough. The charts show a steady climb and a slow fall in spring. At the same time, a poke test left a dent. So the dough is not ready and needs longer.
First, we checked the boards. The charts show a steady bow and a slow fall in stiffness. At the same time, a moisture test read high. So the boards are not ready and need drying.

units.rhetorical_move: the difference is written, the figures are read, three short sentences land the conclusion, and d is set
units.function: show the transform, read the new figures, and state the order that follows
units.reusable_pattern: Let [difference]. From [figures] we observe [behavior]. Thus [no defect]. So [stationary]. Since [method], [order] = [value].
prohibited_generalizations: do not set the order before the figures
do not report a p-value the paper only calls close to zero
units.source_excerpt: the p-values of the unit root test are all close to 0. Thus, there is no unit root. So {gt} and {bt} are stationary sequences. Since we performed a first-order difference method, d = 1

original_instantiations: Let the dough rest once. From the new charts it sits flat and springs back. The poke test now reads low. So the dough is ready. Since we rested it once, the rest count is one.
Let the boards dry once. From the new charts they sit flat and read even. The moisture now reads low. So the boards are ready. Since we dried them once, the drying count is one.

units.rhetorical_move: the order is chosen by computing one criterion over a loop and taking the minimum, and the prediction is named right after
units.function: say how an order is selected and what is computed once it is
units.reusable_pattern: According to [data], we calculate [criterion] under different orders through [loop], and find the order that makes [criterion] the smallest. After that, we [estimate] and calculate [prediction].
prohibited_generalizations: do not name the order the loop found when the paper never prints it
do not skip from the criterion to the prediction
units.source_excerpt: we calculate the BIC value of the model under different orders through the computer programming loop, and find the order p and q that make the BIC the smallest

original_instantiations: From the log, we score each rest time and keep the one with the best score. After that, we bake and record the rise.
From the log, we score each glue and keep the one with the best score. After that, we clamp and record the hold.

units.rhetorical_move: a test is motivated by what a passing residual means, then the statistic is named
units.function: say what the test decides before naming the statistic
units.reusable_pattern: In order to [purpose], a [test] is required. If [condition], it means [interpretation]. We use [statistic].
prohibited_generalizations: do not name the statistic before saying what passing means
